reviews.text:
Excellent experience. It’s restaurant week and date night, a great combination. We had reservations and in my typical style, well 70% of the time, we were 10 minutes late. We called and no worries, they held our reservation. Love that they offer self-parking without even seeing a valet. I’m always a bit embarrassed to tell them that I prefer to self park, but I don’t like someone I don’t know driving my 500hp car, Ferris Bueller flashbacks. The resort is beautiful. Even walking in from the parking garage is extremely classy. See picture. When the elevator reaches the 5th floor it opens directly into the foyer of the restaurant. It’s like arriving at a private penthouse, really cool.

The inside is extremely well decorated, modern, spacious and beautiful. Hostess was super friendly and sat us up against the floor to ceiling glass wall overlooking the city from up on Camelback Mountain, the view was phenomenal, city lights as far as you can see. See pics. All the tables are set beautifully, candle, Pinot wine glasses, full settings. Nice! We grabbed a Tito’s and soda along with a Beam and Seven, great start and went nicely with unlimited homemade fresh warm salted rolls with muffin like tops and homemade butter. Mmmmm!

During restaurant week, we paid $44 per person and each selected from a starter, an entree and a dessert. Check out the special restaurant-week menu picture. We started with the Warm Green Asparagus Salad and the Longevity Noodles. Asparagus was served cold and par cooked, a little smoky, covered in delicious sauce and seasonings. The Noodles were fantastic. 4 grilled shrimp, ginger consommé, homemade al dente noodles, greens, delicious! The menu didn’t say it came with cilantro, which I hate, and they graciously replaced it without even a blink. Super well handled and the manager even came to check on us, no worries. Starters were great! I would normally not order a sirloin steak in any restaurant, but it was the only steak on the restaurant week menu, so we both gave it a shot. So glad we did! One was rare and the other was medium rare, both cooked perfectly, juicy, warm and probably the best sirloin steak I’ve ever had. Typically not a terrific cut of meat, but these were excellent. We also ordered a side of wild mushrooms, they were incredible, not trenched in any kind of butter, garlic or other sauce, the natural flavors shined through and they were terrificThe Japanese eggplant was phenomenal, relatively soft, lightly smoky, fresh and flavorful. See the pics. Dessert was the “chocolate cake” which turned out to be a chocolate lava cake with caramel ice cream and a candied Brulé crisp, fantastic! Mine was carrot cake pie. Never heard of it, but how can you go wrong with carrot cake that’s also a pie?! Lemon cream cheese frosting served with a sweet carrot reduction sauce. Oh, and toasted coconut ice cream! It was phenomenal! Soft, warm, rich, creamy,....mmmmmm! Check out the pics.

Service was excellent. We wanted for nothing and were promptly, yet unobtrusively taken care of by about 4 people plus our server. Everyone was extremely friendly and professional. Very well done!

Overall, this was a terrific value at $44 per person. Bill was $126 including a couple drinks and all. Would it be a 5 star review at $250? Probably not, but this was great. It’s not Kai, but I don’t think it tries to be. It’s high-end, classy, comfortable, modern, clean with fantastic views overlooking an amazing property with high quality food and excellent service. Couldn’t ask for much more.

I would absolutely return and recommend you try it too.

reviews.text:
J&G Steakhouse at the Phoenician – Elevated Dining with a Minor Letdown

We recently dined at J&G Steakhouse at the Phoenician, and the experience was overall very good, with standout food, excellent service, and just one disappointing detail worth noting.

To start, we shared the French onion soup. The kitchen thoughtfully split it for us, which was a nice touch and set the tone for the night. The soup was warm, flavorful, and satisfying — not the best I’ve had, but definitely a solid and comforting way to begin the meal.

Following that, we had the black truffle cheese fritters — six in total. These were outstanding. Rich, hot, and savory with plenty of truffle flavor, they were a highlight. That said, you do need to enjoy truffle to fully appreciate them, but for us, they were a hit.

For the main course, we both ordered the 19-ounce bone-in ribeye, cooked medium-rare. Haley’s steak came out perfect — beautifully seared and full of aged flavor. Unfortunately, mine arrived very overdone, more of a medium-well. While the staff promptly took it back and corrected it, the recook took about 15–20 minutes. While I appreciate that they got it right the second time, I was a little surprised that nothing was offered — no comped dessert or gesture — for the extended wait and initial miss, especially at a restaurant of this caliber.

We finished the night by sharing the carrot cake, and I have to say, it was a pleasant surprise. I’m not usually a carrot cake person, but this one was moist, well-balanced, and absolutely delicious — a great way to end the meal.

Final Thoughts:
Service was excellent throughout — attentive and professional. The food was mostly outstanding, and the atmosphere was what you’d expect from a fine dining spot at the Phoenician. While the mishap with my steak did dampen the flow of the evening, it was handled well, and overall, I’d still recommend J&G for a high-quality steakhouse experience. Just a little more attention to recovery would’ve made it flawless.

reviews.text:
WOW!! I can easily say this was hands down the best fine dining experience my partner and I have ever experienced in our six years together!!

We were immediately greeted with smiles and they congratulated us on our anniversary. They even made us a little card and just made us feel like rock stars the whole time. We had a beautiful table right next to the window with a to die for sunset view.

Our wait staff was phenomenal, very funny and charming and helpful with suggestions. I ordered the passionfruit peach spritz and I would definitely recommend that if you’re looking for a tropical and refreshing drink.

THE FOOD, man, the food was just fantastic. I joked with my boyfriend that I wish I had another stomach because everything tasted so amazing.

We ordered the truffle fries and the shrimp cocktail for apps. They were VERY generous with the portion of fries, it was a large bowl and they were covered in a delicious amount of shaved truffle. 10/10 recommend! The shrimp were also very large and delicious, loved the cocktail and miso dipping sauce for them!! 9/10 for sure!!

For my entree I got the salmon with mashed potatoes and it was perfectly cooked and very flavorful. My partner got the steak and the sauces that came with it were also out of this world.

The complimentary bread was nice and airy!

At the end of the night one of the managers even offered us outside and took some photos of us, it was all so sweet.

Just hands down the most memorable and lovely dinner I’ve ever had, and I would recommend this phenomenal establishment to anyone!!!

reviews.text:
This place was beautiful! I took my husband here for a birthday/dinner date and this couldn't have been a better choice. Upon setting my reservation I did mention it was his birthday and that I would enjoy a table with a beautiful view of outside(so we could watch the sunset) and let me tell you! Once we got in, the first thing the host did was greet my husband with a "Happy Birthday !" Then walked us to our table where the view was just perfect. I love looking at the city during the night time and where we were seated gave us the most perfect "lookout" view. Our waiters were top tier. Taking into consideration any food allergies they made sure we still were able to enjoy our food and the experience without fail. Our dinner was superb, our drinks so good, and then to top it off they surprised my husband with a Happy birthday dessert that was just so beautiful. reviews.text:
For all the hype, the experience of eating at J&G is incredibly lack-luster.

The staff is incredibly enthusiastic and friendly, and the service was exceptional.

There was live music in the bar area, which at first seemed great. However, we were seated fairly far away and the music was still so loud it was difficult to carry a conversation at the table without constantly asking each other to repeat what was just said.

The menu is really why this steakhouse is not my favorite. Nothing on this menu stands out as signature to the restaurant or special. We may as well have eaten at Outback for a quarter of the price.

The kids menu is incredibly basic: pasta, grilled cheese, chicken. There are no options for children to have a high quality meal unless you order from the adult menu.

We got the chilled shellfish platter to start. It looked lovely, but really was not great. The condiments were lacking and overall this dish was a disappointment.

At our table we got the salmon and two different steaks Oscar style, grilled asparagus and roasted mushrooms. Everything was cooked alright, nothing was over the top delicious.

We passed on desert as nothing really stood out.

Overall, we had a nice time and decent food, but we will not be returning. This restaurant did not impress. There are plenty of other options in the area that have the wow-factor this restaurant is missing.

One of the best steaks that I have had in the desert. Visiting town from Los Angeles for the weekend so we wanted a special place to have a great dinner. I have stayed at the Phoenician a few times before so have known about J&G for quite a while but last night was our first time trying it. It has great views of the valley and is very large and open on the inside. They have a large and long bar with live music on one side and then a lot of seating options next to that. We reserved a booth by the window however there was a booking issue so we had to sit at another table. Our server was very polite and prompt, and made up for the seating mishap a bit.

I chose the Heirloom Tomatoes with Roasted Peaches, and the Filet Mignon 12oz. The heirloom tomatoes were very tasty although the dish was very small in portion size. I wouldn’t really call it an appetizer, it is more a starter or tapas sized portion. The steak, however, was delicious and cooked perfectly. Definitely one of the better steaks that I’ve had in the desert and I would certainly order it again.

Overall a really great dinner with great service and a great steak. The only issue we had was the seating mishap, but aside from that it was a great dinner overall and I would definitely recommend it.

reviews.text: We arrived at 7:15p for our 7:30 reservation party of 9. We were seated on time, got our first round of drinks going, and they gave us  complimentary appetizers due to event coordinator error prior to booking. I typically write great reviews especially for the waiting staff because I appreciate their dedication to customer satisfaction. However, I’m unsure if we were just too big of a table or if our waiter just felt flustered on the slow Monday night. We ended up waiting for our food for 2 hours. We ordered around 8p, they close at 9, and we got our food around 10:05p. The table next to ours with 6 people who arrived an hour after we did was served before us. When we finally got our food, it was cooked well, kind of bland but the sauces helped with that. Some of the food we ordered didn’t come out and when we asked the waiter about it he replied they were out of the item (could have told us when we ordered it). One of our guests ordered a lemon drop martini and he brought out a passion fruit drink and insisted it was a lemon drop even though we told him it wasn’t. We got a desert for our birthday guest and they forgot her candle so we had to remind them even though there were balloons at the table. And finally, they advise they would be able to split the bill on 2 checks, but the waiter seemed flustered again as he appeared to be confused on how to split the check. We just had him put everything on one check because we were all tired and ready to leave at this point. Needless to say we will not be going back and we’re very unsatisfied with this “fine dining” experience! We did get some great photos of the view at least.

reviews.text:
This is a perfect special occasion spot! The restaurant is gorgeous, the food is well prepared, and the service is 5-star. I'd recommend a reservation for this spot as meals here can take a while. From sitting down to paying the bill it was a total of 2.5 hours. For me that's an eternity, but in this case it was time well spent.

The restaurant is huge with one of the best views of Phoenix I've ever seen. All of the tables are positioned to admire the south facing view of Downtown Phoenix and Tempe. I was very impressed!

A lot of the food here is very generic to other steak houses but they tend to push the seafood here more than anything else. If seafood is your thing you gotta come here! I'm not that big of a fan of shellfish and wanted to try out a few of the different options on the menu. Fortunately they had a pre fixed menu option that came with:
Truffle potato fritters that were basically croquets,
Tuna tartare (a local favorite apparently),
Mushroom risotto,
Entree of 1/2 Lobster and a filet mignon,
Dessert of chocolate lava cake.
All for $99 so we decided to go for this option!

We decided to sub the filet mignon for an 8 oz cut of the prime New York strip. The staff was in a bit of an uproar, they'd never heard of someone wanting to sub out the filet. Eventually, as you can see from the pics they were able to accommodate. I'd definitely recommend it cause the New York Strip was amazing. It's always been my experience that Filet Mignon is pretty underwhelming.

I'd do the pre fix menu again but it'd be nice to get a different dessert next time. Chocolate lava cake just reminds me of Jack in the Box drive thru.

If you need a spot to propose, to take out your parents, or to just feel special for a night, I'd recommend this J&G Steak house.

reviews.text:
Okay, I can't beat up on J&G because the service and atmosphere are amazing. Very knowledgeable staff, very attentive and not obtrusive. The 180 degree views are sme of the best in the valley, especially if there is a storm rolling in.. allegedly;)
Now for the food... ughhhhh.... never had tasteless lobster and served without butter of any kind. Some pieces were down right rubbery. The "bread" was something you get from the freezer section and put in a cupcake tin to cook... equally tasteless and served with the most plain butter I've ever had. Zero taste at all. So I ask the server and explain how bland everything has been so if I want a flavorful steak (since they don't serve any style of pork chop) what would I order. He recommends the bone in ribeye and I bite... even after he explains how they don't use much spice and when he cools his burgers he doesn't even use salt n pepper... what the what.... but okay...
So the ribeye was good.. not great but I felt like the seasoning was good and that what I enjoyed. The most anorexic 19oz bone in I've ever had and not even properly trimmed. The lobster Mac was the star and let me just say... it was velveta with flavorless lobster chuncks and shell store bought shells. Just not the quality you expect when spending over $350 for 2 people and we split a $52 bottle of Malbec... I give everyone a chance and even provide real-time feedback and don't expect excuses. I expect appropriate response... nonetheless.. we got exceptional photos and of course my wife provided amazing company. I have to say... even the espresso martini was like sweet dirt! No wonder why we were a le to make same day reservations for sunset. There are better options with better quality for a quarter of the price... Heck save the money and got to Rustlers Roost if it views you want. Or go to Maple & Ash if you want top quality and no view for less but feel like VIP. See where I'm going here.... Totally missed the mark and could care less. They were out of sparkling water, charged $8 which is normal.price but brought a small bottle and the 2nd bottle was included in the price but they never brought it out tableside... okay... enough... I hate to leave negative reviews... moving on!

Pass if you are looking for an overall Great experince with food. Opt for Modern oyster bar or steak 44 instead, better portions and same or similar pricing. reviews.text:
We came here for our wedding anniversary and will never return. It was a Tuesday night and not busy at all.

Service was great, a little slow, water refilled often, but they never asked us what the occasion was and seemed like they were just waiting to go home. 4/5

Food was mediocre and unseasoned - with the exception of the seabass. The food barely even had salt on it, no pepper, no flavor. It was shockingly underwhelming after the word of mouth reviews and the view. We ordered the 19 oz steak, seabass, Brussels sprouts, and a baked potato.

Steak arrived lukewarm like it had been sitting for a while. No flavor. I thought the steak would have been the most flavorful. 2/5

The seabass was the highlight of the meal. Well cooked and seasoned, loved the plating and sauces. Portion was small even for me as someone who doesn't eat much. 4/5

Listed as caramelized Brussels sprouts with pecans, we were received Brussels sprouts that looked steamed or boiled, no flavor aside from a pinch of salt, few drops of balsamic vinegar, and some dry pecans thrown on top. 1/5

The baked potato was very dry and came with bacon bits that smelled like dog food. 1/5

10 years ago I'm sure it was a lot better. Really disappointing. Save your money ($170 for two entrees and two sides) and go somewhere else on Camelback. reviews.text: Amazing birthday dinner from start to finish! Our waiter, Jeff, made it extra special with his friendly personality and attentive but not intrusive manner. My husband’s Bulleit Rye old-fashioned was made perfectly. The pomegranate Cosmopolitan was good but not my favorite. Not enough of a fruit flavor in my opinion but plenty strong! The Moscow mule was much better. A crab cake appetizer was generous and perfect for two...flaky and flavorful with a delicious citrus sauce. My sea bass was spectacular (thank you Jeff for the recommendation) along with a side of cheesy and creamy gratin potatoes, and my husband’s prime Ribeye was huge and cooked to perfection, paired with three sauces (on the side) and a side of  sautéed mushrooms. The sides are generous and can be shared by 2-3 people, and fresh warm rolls were a nice complimentary add-on. We finished off our meal with a wonderful warm apple cobbler. The tart green apple with sweet crumble topping and vanilla ice cream was so good! We also enjoyed a beautiful view of the Arizona sunset. Can’t wait to visit J&G again!

reviews.text:
Context: This was my first visit to J&G 1/21/2021

I've never had a better experience at any restaurant, period. The staff is phenomenal and that is probably an understatement.

Specifically four people:

Melissa aka (Long Island Lady) was the hostess and she made us feel welcome immediately. We had a good laugh about family in New York and she started off what was a perfect evening with a smile.

Austin was our server and he is super dope! Incredibly knowledgeable, professional, yet human. It wasn't like dealing with a robot.

He knew the products without hesitation, but he also was able to speak to us on a humble and real level? Most importantly, he knew how to make my wife feel comfortable and we will be regulars simply because of his outstanding service. He is literally like talking to your friend of several years.

Hector was the person bringing bread and clearing the table. If you blinked your table would be free of used dishes and spotless.

I asked him his name and he was kind and professional. We began to speak and it was
refreshing to speak with such a kind soul.

Kevin is one of the managers and he was incredible. He stopped by to ask how our experience was; however, he genuinely wanted to know and we conversed about several things.

He provided a desert that my wife loved and while such a simple act, we appreciated the service and he belongs in management. Management is essentially managing humans and he has excellent human interaction skills.

He bridged the gap between professionalism and humanity perfectly.

Of course, you all want to know about the food. 11 out of 10!!!! I recommend the wagyu ribeye and the black truffle cheese fritters, but be careful, they're addictive!

Can't wait to go back.

Only bad part; We had made a reservation a day in advance for patio seating at 530, unfortunately when we got there they told us it would be about another 20 mins of a wait due to a wedding reception. reviews.text:
In a word: Excellent.

My friends and I took a bachelor party trip to AZ for Spring Training and we came across J&G. When we arrived, the hostess let us know that our table should be ready shortly. 20-30 minutes passed and we were finally seated. It was a rainy night in AZ so I think diners were staying a bit longer than normal.

While I would normally condemn a place for seating me 30m late, the response was too amazing not to come on here and write about it. When we were seated, the waiter, Jeff, informed us that we would be receiving a complimentary appetizer for the wait. This gesture alone likely would've sufficed but the manager came to our table shortly after and said that the first round of drinks would also be complimentary. We were quite satisfied at this point with the apology. Over the course of dinner, Jeff was amazing. If you decide to go, you should request a table of his. He saw to every detail/request with ease. Just impeccable service.

So, the bill finally arrived after a 2+ hour meal and we discovered that the restaurant had comped ALL of our drinks. This apology more than made up for the wait. We were all floored.

I guess I should probably talk about the food too. It was incredible. Everything we tried was amazing. Too many things to list. Request Jeff and ask him what to get. He will not steer you wrong. Bravo J&G!

Unfortunately there was one additional incident that was more disturbing. We paid with our credit card and when the waiter returned after running the card, he didn't give back our credit card. He said he had forgot, but it's very hard to believe he would go run the credit card and forget to return it moments later. reviews.text: I just wanted to write about my experience at J&G Steakhouse.  My mom is visiting from Wisconsin, and we wanted to take her out for a nice birthday dinner and were excited to take her to J&G. The lady at the check-in desk was wonderful, as usual, and welcomed us.  My husband and I have dined at J&G multiple times so she recognized us and was warm and welcome. I thought it would be a good indication of the rest of our time there, but that wasn’t the case. Our waiter was really bad, when he initially came to take our order, we said we would need another minute; he came back approximately 20 minutes later.  Throughout the evening, we barely saw him, and toward the end of our meal, once our plates were cleared, and he knew we were finished and ready to go, we sat there for probably another 20-30 minutes waiting for our check.  It was so bad that we contemplated getting up and asking the front desk for our check instead. We came in right at opening, and it was not that busy. The worst part is he was focused on the table right beside us, and it was pretty obvious he was showing them preferential treatment. My husband and I asked the waiter if the chicken Parmesan were enough for my husband and I to split since we were already getting an appetizer, he said yes, so we did.  My husband’s portion was not good at all, and he was surprised that J&G would serve chicken like it. He had the dark chicken thigh portion, and I had the white chicken, he said the chicken thigh tasted like school cafeteria meat and he could barely stomach it. I had to give him some of my white chicken, so he would not be hungry. The waiter never came to ask how our food was, and was so absent that my husband had to resort to drinking ice water throughout the rest of the meal because he never came to check on refills. My mom ordered a glass of wine, once that was gone, he never asked if she wanted another one. I asked for a window seat in my reservation, which I made weeks ago, and we weren’t seated in front of the window. I have been planning my mom’s birthday dinner for weeks since she is only in town for a short time, and I was really hoping J&G would go above and beyond my expectations, I will definitely be picking a different place next time. Obviously the new management that took over the Phoenician do not care about their customers.  I wrote them over a week ago with my experience and they never responded, the old management cared about the service they provided and if there was a problem, they reached out and did things to rectify the situation so they wouldn't lose customers.

reviews.text:
Beautiful restaurant! We went there for our 1st wedding anniversary, and sat on the patio. Views are lovely, atmosphere was great. A hand-written card from the Manager was a really neat touch.

Service was PERFECT, and I can't stress this enough! I am particularity picky, having worked in a five diamond resort for 10 years, 4 of which were in fine restaurants, so I always notice more things than my company cares for. :) Our server was very attentive, knowledgeable of the menu, both personable and professional, but he was not hovering over us too much. There is nothing I find more annoying (and this normally happens in fine restaurants), than your server making your entire evening into his/her recital, or asking how your food is before you even had the chance to taste it. Everyone at the restaurant we interacted with greeted us with a warm smile, and was helpful. Timeliness of service was impeccable: table was cleared on time, courses went out just on time, but not too soon to make us feel rushed.

Food was also lovely. Tuna tartar looked beautiful, and my husband liked it. I had the squash soup, which was so flavorful, and the presentation was great. It breaks my hart that I could not have steak, as I like mine medium rare, but am pregnant. That's all right, I lived vicariously trough my husband, and my fish was delicious. He says his steak was phenomenal: perfectly cooked and seasoned. I tried the sauces (they brought three different ones, as were indecisive), and all were great. The sides were delicious too. The only thing I did not love, was the side of mac n' cheese, but this comes from the self-professed mac n' cheese snob (I really prefer strong creamy cheeses, and I feel cheddar is derived from some sort of plastic).

Prices were OK for a restaurant of this rating, and especially considering the generous portions. Their most expensive steak is the Porterhouse ($60.00), and it is absolutely HUGE (24 oz). Priced and portioned for two really.

Deserts was beautifully presented, (we received complimentary carrot cake). Though I am not a huge fan of carrot cake, this one was delicious. I also liked the mango and carrot sorbet on it (which I think they are making from scratch, and the carrot one was brilliant).

All in all, great restaurant, well worth the price and I highly recommend it.

- Bojana H.
